label: IN_ACT_4, mode of possession left open: the grades frame field GradesFrame.InAct
term: in act, mode of possession left open
definition: `GradesFrame.InAct x r`: x actually has the perfection r, as fire is actually hot, with the mode of possession (formal, virtual or eminent) left open. It is the primitive of DEF-ACT taken as one shared relation: DISAMB-IN-ACT records that every act premise of the case uses the one parameter `InAct`, so that within a result every premise is read in the same sense and the formal or virtual determination is a question of premise truth, not of validity. IN_ACT_1 (formal), IN_ACT_2 (virtual) and IN_ACT_3 (formal or virtual) are candidate determinations of it; no statement relates them to it.
note: Stipulative frame-field record, attribution deferred; its content is DEF-ACT (sourced through the motion and q.4 a.1 claims). It is a separate record so that tagging binders with IN_ACT_4 does not retroactively assign a sense to the arguments whose statements link DEF-ACT: two of them (the in-act sense fork summary and the GOD_4 PERFECT_2 route) already link IN_ACT_1 and IN_ACT_2 definitions as well, and DEF-ACT as a sense would add a third sense to each without a recorded bridge. Merging this record into DEF-ACT is a follow-up that needs those arguments reviewed for sense_bridges. Introduced with the grades frame module (TruthCore/Causality/GradesFrame.lean) after the truth discover diagnosis of 2026-11-20.

formal_gap.meaning: GradesFrame.InAct x r says that the being x actually has the perfection r. A model supplies the relation; Lean fixes only its type. It does not say whether x has r in its own kind (formally) or as a cause able to produce it (virtually, eminently).
examples: A fire is in act as to heat (r being hot).
Read at esse, InAct x esse says that x has being (DEF-ESSE).
exclusions: Being in potency to r (InPotency): a thing in potency to heat is not thereby in act as to heat; their non-simultaneity in one respect is an explicit premise, not part of this field.
Moving or causing (MovesIn, CausesIn): having a perfection is not producing it in another.
A definite mode of possession: formal act (IN_ACT_1), virtual act (IN_ACT_2) and their disjunction (IN_ACT_3) are separate senses.
open_obligations: No law relating InAct to InPotency, MoreIn or CausesIn follows from the field; each is an explicit premise where used.
A defence of the act premises must fix one determination and defend all of them in it (DISAMB-IN-ACT).
No formalization candidate from more basic vocabulary: InAct is a basic relation of the family.
